referents.why: 'for them' (autois), plural: the crowd, a collective noun that takes plural pronouns. It is the only candidate that can be the people asking.
'he did for them' (as usual) is Pilate's custom. The builder's w5 is 'to beg', an infinitive, not a person.
referents.category: implied subject; builder pointed at an infinitive

links.why: Self-link: a clause cannot follow itself.
The participle having gone up is nested in the leading clause.
links.category: antecedent participle nested in main clause

links.why: The infinitive is the object of 'began': an infinitive completing the main verb, nested by the grammar.
Kathos, 'just as he always did': the asking is compared to the custom, a clause nested in the prepositional role.
